dog.now.why: proprio is the spoken clip of propriétaire. A person drops by with passer; visiter is for places. Both doors take a bare infinitive.

dog.past.why: Two different pasts: voulait is imparfait for an intention, while j'ai dû is passé composé because the hiding actually happened.

dog.neg.why: je ne dois pas would mean I must not, so no-need becomes n'ai pas besoin de (have no need to). Speech drops both ne: veut pas, j'ai pas besoin.

dog.q.why: No question marker and no do: the second half keeps statement order and only the voice rises. Est-ce que tu dois... is the careful version.

cant.now.why: Spoken French says on, not nous, with a singular verb (peut). hid becomes passé composé ont caché, and parce que leaves word order alone.

cant.past.why: pas slips between a and pu. The hiding happened before the not-coming, so it moves back a step to plus-que-parfait: avaient caché.

cant.fut.why: No be-able-to swap: pouvoir simply takes the futur simple ending, pourra, and ne ... pas wraps that one word.

cant.although.why: quand même sits between door and infinitive, like still. Spoken même si keeps the indicative; bien que would force the subjunctive aient caché.

like.now.why: The sister stays the subject, unlike Spanish. The liked thing takes le: le café means coffee in general, not a cup of it.

like.neg.why: ne elides to n' before aime and pas follows the door. The article stays le after aimer, not de. Speech drops n': elle aime pas le café.

like.they.why: Plural is written on mes and aiment, but the -ent is silent: aiment sounds exactly like aime, so only mes (not ma) is heard.

like.q.why: est-ce que is a frozen question opener: after it the order is plain statement order. Tu aimes le café ? with rising pitch is equally common.

go.habit.why: à + le fuses into au. every Sunday is plural with an article, tous les dimanches; le dimanche alone would also mean on Sundays.

go.prog.why: No progressive: ils vont is both they go and they are going, so là (right now) does the work. en train d'aller exists but is heavy for a trip.

go.past.why: aller takes être, not avoir, so the participle agrees with ils: allés, with a silent -s. Two women would be elles sont allées.

go.fut.why: Futur simple on the irregular stem ir- + -ont: tense is a suffix, not a word. ils vont au marché demain is just as spoken.

go.neg.why: No auxiliary and no -ing: ne ... pas wraps the plain present vont. Speech: ils vont pas au marché aujourd'hui.

live.now.why: Present tense plus depuis: no perfect, no auxiliary. habite is the plain he lives form; depuis alone says it started and still goes on.

live.past.why: Finished stretch, so passé composé with avoir, and depuis switches to pendant. Speech often drops pendant: il a habité à Delhi deux ans.

live.fut.why: Not a future perfect: the future goes onto ça fera (it will make), que links, and habite stays present. il aura habité sounds written.

live.q.why: The question phrase stays at the end, where depuis deux ans would sit, and the verb is plain present. No have, no been, no -ing.

rain.now.why: The empty il stays, but is raining is one word, pleut. The order uses the tu form prends with no pronoun; alors is the everyday spoken so.

rain.fut.why: Futur proche matches going to piece for piece: va carries the tense, pleuvoir stays infinitive. il pleuvra sounds like a weather forecast.

rain.neg.why: The order is ne prends pas, and after a negation un becomes de: pas de parapluie. Speech drops ne: il pleut pas, prends pas de parapluie.

if.real.why: si + present, futur simple in the main clause: the -ra ending is all of English will. Spoken on replaces nous, so both verbs are singular.

if.unreal.why: si + imparfait (avait), conditionnel (voyagerait) in the main clause. Never si + conditionnel: les si n'aiment pas les -rait.

if.past.why: Both clauses are avoir + participle: plus-que-parfait avait eu after si, conditionnel passé aurait voyagé in the main. Only avoir's tense changes.
